question.text: Chapter 9 contrasts 'an idea' vs 'an opportunity'. An opportunity has proven commercial value AND can generally break-even within how many months from ideation, per Chapter 9?

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'An idea has the potential to become an opportunity and a viable enterprise, if it has the potential to break even, generally within 36 months from ideation, has a passionate and dedicated team developing the idea, faces manageable risks and can forecast high gross margins.' The Trap: Option A is too tight (most start-ups cannot break even in 1 year). Options C and D extend the break-even too far — at 60+ months most funds would write off the idea. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covered the 36-month benchmark. XV uses break-even horizon in start-up coverage.
